data.title: Insecure Data Storage in Mobile Application
data.summary: The mobile application stored authentication tokens and personal data in unprotected locations on the device, recoverable from a backup or from a device an attacker holds.
data.description:
Mobile platforms provide protected storage — Keychain and Keystore — which binds secrets to the device and optionally to user authentication. Data written outside it, to preferences files, local databases or the filesystem, carries only the protection of the app sandbox.

The sandbox fails in the cases that matter: a rooted or jailbroken device, an unencrypted backup, a forensic extraction, or malware with elevated access. Tokens recovered this way are often long-lived, so a device examined once yields account access indefinitely.

Caches are the overlooked part: screenshots taken on backgrounding, WebView caches, logs and crash reports frequently contain the data the application was careful about elsewhere.
data.recommendation:
* Store credentials and tokens in the platform keystore, requiring user authentication to release them where appropriate.
* Keep personal data out of plaintext files and databases; encrypt with keys held in the keystore.
* Exclude sensitive files from cloud and local backups.
* Suppress sensitive content in task-switcher snapshots, and keep it out of logs and crash reports.
* Keep token lifetimes short and support remote revocation.
data.short_recommendation: Store secrets in the platform keystore, not in app storage.
